coarse_skill_concept: Refactoring a serial computation to execute in parallel using Python multiprocessing (ProcessPoolExecutor) or a compiled parallelism layer, then benchmarking the resulting speedup.

task_judgments.reason: The task is exactly the candidate skill: identify a per-file embarrassingly-parallel unit (PBKDF2), wrap it in a Python worker, distribute via ProcessPoolExecutor, collect results, and verify a wall-clock speedup gate.

The task requires implementing O(n) spatial-binning physics in C++ and applying OpenMP pragmas plus MPI inter-process communication—a fundamentally different skill from Python process-pool task distribution over embarrassingly-parallel items.

final_groups.skill_concept: Parallelising an embarrassingly-parallel per-item computation in Python by wrapping a worker function in ProcessPoolExecutor, collecting futures, and validating wall-clock speedup against a serial baseline.
final_groups.reasoning: The task fits this skill exactly: enumerate files, submit one process task per file via ProcessPoolExecutor, sort and serialise results, and satisfy a t_par <= 0.70*t_seq gate.

final_groups.skill_concept: Implementing a 2D particle simulator with O(n) spatial binning in C++ and then parallelising it in two distinct compiled-parallelism paradigms: OpenMP shared-memory (pragma annotations) and MPI distributed-memory (process ranks with halo communication), then comparing all three via summary timing files.
final_groups.reasoning: The dominant challenge is the physics-correct spatial-binning kernel and the two different C++ parallelism models (OpenMP vs MPI); Python multiprocessing plays no role and the parallelism patterns (shared-memory loop-level vs distributed-memory domain decomposition) are completely distinct from ProcessPoolExecutor task farming.
